Timeline::add_minutes¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline Timeline::add_minutes(int minutes) const

Add Fixed Elapsed Minutes¶

add_minutes() adds a scalar number of exact 60-second intervals to every defined instant. It is designed for delays, timeouts, lead times, and clock adjustments naturally expressed as an integral minute count.

The operation adds minutes * 60,000,000,000 nanoseconds on the epoch axis. It does not round the input to a minute and does not clear seconds or fractional seconds. Use floor when quantization is the goal.

Example 1. Adding two minutes crosses both midnight and the year boundary while preserving seconds and all nine fractional digits.

const auto source = pluss::timeline::make(
    "2024-12-31T23:59:30.123456789Z");
std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::timeline::format(
    source.add_minutes(2), "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"2025-01-01T00:01:30.123456789+00:00"

Direction, Zero, And Mutation¶

Positive values move later, negative values move earlier, and zero leaves each instant unchanged. A new timeline is returned in every case; the source is not modified.

Example 2. Negative and zero counts have direct signed meanings.

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::timeline::format(
    source.add_minutes(-2), "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';
std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::timeline::format(
    source.add_minutes(0), "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"2024-12-31T23:57:30.123456789+00:00"
Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"2024-12-31T23:59:30.123456789+00:00"

Shape, Timezone, And Absence¶

The scalar count applies to every logical element without changing rank or shape. The timezone label is retained and may cause a transition-crossing result to display with a different UTC offset. NaT stays NaT; empty inputs remain empty; strided borrowed storage is read correctly.

Example 3. A matrix remains a matrix and preserves absence.

const auto values = pluss::timeline::make({
    {"2024-01-01T09:00:00Z", "2024-01-01T09:30:15.000000004Z"},
    {"", "2024-01-01T23:59:45Z"},
});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::timeline::format(
    values.add_minutes(1), "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["2024-01-01T09:01:00.000000000+00:00", "2024-01-01T09:31:15.000000004+00:00"], 
  ["NaT", "2024-01-02T00:00:45.000000000+00:00"]
]

Range Validation¶

Both the unit-to-nanosecond conversion and each epoch addition are checked. The method throws if either would exceed signed 64-bit epoch storage; it never wraps into an unrelated date.

Example 4. An unrepresentable scaled count is rejected.

try {
  (void)pluss::timeline::make("1970-01-01T00:00:00Z")
      .add_minutes(2'147'483'647);
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "rejected\n";
}

Output¶

rejected
